messages:
tara: Finance flagged two customers with duplicate billing on streaming calls that included a mid-stream tool invocation. Not huge, but reproducible. Filed FIN-412. Anyone seen this pattern?
ben: We saw a similar trace in staging. Root cause looked like: stream truncated -> client reconnect -> router re-routes to different shard -> toolcall executed again because no stable id.
lucy: Do we have any dedupe at the ledger for provisional credits across routes? I thought tombstones handled it.
tara: Tombstones exist but are keyed by route-instance + toolcall-id. When the router changes route the tombstone key differs so nothing dedupes.
omar: Yikes. What's the call graph? Can you paste the trace?
tara: pasted trace:
```
[router] start session session=usr_722 route=canary-03
[runtime] stream up to offset=1024
[client] got EOF/timeout
[router] client reconnect -> route=stable-01
[runtime] resume with prefix-cached
[app] toolcall execute() (id header missing)
[ledger] provisional +35 tokens acct=acct_99 ref=protoX
```
Later same flow ran earlier toolcall and ledger had another +35.
ben: Key insight: runtime relies on client-supplied toolcall id. If absent, toolrunner treats it as new. Two commits -> two finals.
lucy: Two quick mitigation ideas: 1) runtime-synthesized canonical id based on normalized prefix (tokenized) + tool-name; 2) ledger-side short TTL cross-route tombstone that keys on acct + prefix-hash + tool-name.
omar: For (1) we need a canonicalization step: encode prefix using our tokenizer (BPE) and compute sha1 of first N tokens. That will be stable across resumes where prefix cache is identical.
tara: Be careful: some resumptions use different chunk boundaries due to prefetch and chunking; tokenization-based hashing should be stable though. Also cap token count to 512 to bound cost.
ben: Implementation notes: runtime can compute header X-Canonical-Toolcall: sha1(...) and router should forward it unchanged even across routing decisions. toolrunner must use that header as primary id. If header missing, fall back to client id.
lucy: For ledger TTL tombstone, suggest 30s window initially. If duplicate provisional detected within TTL, mark as duplicate and suppress commit, but still emit telemetry so we can audit.
omar: Telemetry: add span tag 'toolcall.dedup_reason' with values {none,client_id,canonical_header,ledger_ttl} and metric 'billing.toolcall_duplicates{model,route,reason}'. We missed signal previously.
tara: UX: Console should show a single logical invocation with a footnote: "this request had multiple provisional attempts; billing credited once after dedupe" when dedupe applied. For already affected customers we need to surface adjustments.
\enfra-bot: FIN-412 created and assigned to eng-platform: https://internal/p/FIN-412
ben: I'll open a PR for router+runtime to forward the canonical header and runtime to compute it when client doesn't provide an id. lucy can you own the ledger tombstone change?
lucy: Yup. I'll also add a reconciliation query to find finalized duplicates in the last 30d for manual audit.
omar: I'll add Grafana panels: billing.toolcall_duplicates and traces list sample. Also a runbook for when Finance pings about duplicated charges.
tara: Thanks. Quick deploy plan: land runtime header + router pass-through behind feature flag; land ledger TTL dedupe in infra; enable feature flag in canary for 5% traffic and monitor metric.
ben: One more edge: toolcall triggered by function-calling style where payload is large. Normalization should trim whitespace and canonicalize JSON keys for stable hashing. We'll add a small normalizer util.
lucy: Good call. Keep me posted on the normalizer changes since ledger dedupe relies on stable canonicalization.
tara: Great. We'll loop back after canary results. If someone wants to pair on a repro, ping me.
